submission.summary:
DOAC dose review for all 6 panel patients on a direct oral anticoagulant for nonvalvular AF. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl calculated from today's age, most recent weight and serum creatinine.

Changed (4):
- pt-2001 Daniel Brooks (62M, 104 kg, SCr 0.7, CrCl ~161 mL/min): edoxaban 60 mg daily is not recommended for NVAF when CrCl >95 mL/min (reduced efficacy vs warfarin). Discontinued edoxaban and started apixaban 5 mg BID (no reduction criteria met).
- pt-2002 Priya Raman (74F, 52 kg, SCr 1.4, CrCl ~29 mL/min): rivaroxaban reduced 20 mg -> 15 mg once daily (labeled dose for CrCl 15-50 mL/min; take with evening meal).
- pt-2003 Walter Novak (78M, 78 kg, SCr 1.7, CrCl ~40 mL/min) on dronedarone (P-gp inhibitor): dabigatran reduced 150 mg BID -> 75 mg BID per label for CrCl 30-50 mL/min with dronedarone.
- pt-2004 Samuel Greene (81M, 88 kg, SCr 1.2): apixaban increased 2.5 mg -> 5 mg BID; only 1 of 3 reduction criteria met, so he was underdosed.

No change needed (2):
- pt-2005 Eleanor Voss (83F, 57 kg, SCr 1.1): meets 2 apixaban reduction criteria (age >=80, weight <=60 kg); 2.5 mg BID is correct.
- pt-2006 Marcus Lee (66M, 95 kg, SCr 1.1, CrCl ~89 mL/min): rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily is correct.

No other medications were altered. Suggest follow-up renal function monitoring, particularly for pt-2002 and pt-2003.

DOAC dose review for all 6 panel patients with nonvalvular AF on a DOAC. CrCl by Cockcroft-Gault using current age, actual body weight and most recent creatinine (all labs within the last month).

Changed (4):
- pt-2001 Daniel Brooks (62M, 104 kg, Cr 0.7, CrCl ~161 mL/min): edoxaban 60 mg daily is not recommended for NVAF when CrCl >95 mL/min (FDA boxed warning, reduced efficacy vs warfarin). Discontinued edoxaban and started apixaban 5 mg twice daily (no reduction criteria met).
- pt-2002 Priya Raman (74F, 52 kg, Cr 1.4, CrCl ~29 mL/min): rivaroxaban reduced 20 mg -> 15 mg once daily (with evening meal) per label for CrCl 15-50 mL/min.
- pt-2003 Walter Novak (78M, 78 kg, Cr 1.7, CrCl ~40 mL/min) on dronedarone: dabigatran reduced 150 mg -> 75 mg twice daily per label for CrCl 30-50 mL/min with concomitant P-gp inhibitor dronedarone.
- pt-2004 Samuel Greene (81M, 88 kg, Cr 1.2): apixaban increased 2.5 mg -> 5 mg twice daily; only 1 of 3 reduction criteria met (age >=80 only), so he was underdosed.

No change needed (2):
- pt-2005 Eleanor Voss (83F, 57 kg, Cr 1.1): apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily correct (age >=80 and weight <=60 kg).
- pt-2006 Marcus Lee (66M, 95 kg, Cr 1.1, CrCl ~89 mL/min): rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily correct.

No other medications were altered. Suggest confirming renal function follow-up and counseling on the rivaroxaban/dabigatran dose changes.

DOAC dose review for all 6 panel patients on a DOAC for nonvalvular AF (pt-2001 to pt-2006). CrCl by Cockcroft-Gault using current weight/creatinine.

Changed (4):
- pt-2001 Daniel Brooks (62M, 104 kg, Cr 0.7, CrCl ~161 mL/min): edoxaban 60 mg daily is not recommended for NVAF when CrCl >95 mL/min (reduced efficacy vs warfarin). Discontinued edoxaban and started apixaban 5 mg BID (no dose-reduction criteria met).
- pt-2002 Priya Raman (74F, 52 kg, Cr 1.4, CrCl ~29 mL/min): rivaroxaban reduced 20 mg -> 15 mg once daily with evening meal per label for CrCl 15-50 mL/min.
- pt-2003 Walter Novak (78M, 78 kg, Cr 1.7, CrCl ~40 mL/min) on dronedarone: dabigatran reduced 150 mg BID -> 75 mg BID per label (CrCl 30-50 mL/min with P-gp inhibitor dronedarone). Note: an edit was briefly applied to the wrong medication ID (atorvastatin) and was immediately reverted to its original 20 mg once daily; no net change to atorvastatin.
- pt-2004 Samuel Greene (81M, 88 kg, Cr 1.2): apixaban increased 2.5 mg -> 5 mg BID; only 1 of 3 reduction criteria met (age >=80 only).

No change (2):
- pt-2005 Eleanor Voss (83F, 57 kg, Cr 1.1): apixaban 2.5 mg BID correct (age >=80 and weight <=60 kg).
- pt-2006 Marcus Lee (66M, 95 kg, Cr 1.1, CrCl ~89 mL/min): rivaroxaban 20 mg daily correct.

No other medications were altered.
